data.name: Krushna
data.gender_notes: Krushna is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Krushna is the eighth avatar of the god Vishnu. Born to destroy the demon king Kamsa, Krushna is known for his strength, mischievousness, and love for butter. He is often depicted as a dark-skinned, all-attracting, and all-powerful deity. The name Krushna carries the meaning “Dark, Black, or All-Attracting” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Krushna usually hope their child will grow to embody dark, black, or all-attracting and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine presence and power to overcome adversity.
data.etymology: Krushna belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dark, Black, or All-Attracting.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Krushna total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
